decisions.statement: The change machinery and the command page type are asked of the index rather than spelled.
The change machinery is looked for as a page type rather than under every page type.
The command page type is looked for as a page type rather than under every page type.
A page of another type carrying that slug is not taken for that page type.
Code inside either page type is passed over.
A change writes there.
A write is a call to a name taken from `node:fs` or `node:fs/promises`.
`Bun.write` is a write too.
A file whose text names neither `fs` nor `Bun.write` is passed over before it is parsed.
The argument judged is the argument a write lands on rather than the argument a write reads.
A rename is judged on both its paths.
A rename empties the path that rename leaves.
The checkout root is read off a `root` field or taken from the module answering that root.
A name built from a rooted name is rooted whether declared or assigned later.
Whatever the repository ignores is read from `.gitignore` rather than named here.
That `.gitignore` is read as the change leaves it rather than as the disk holds it.
A change taking `.gitignore` away leaves nothing but `.git` ignored.
A rule is read as the name left once its stars and its edging slashes are gone.
`.git` is ignored though no rule names `.git`.
A name built from a name spelling an ignored name spells that name too.
Only a page's code is judged.
The tree a test sets up is no reach.
A destination is refused where the destination is rooted and names nothing ignored.
Making a directory writes no body.
`mkdir` is no write.
A name `node:os` answers is away from the checkout.
A name built from such a name is away from the checkout too.
The value a function answers with is read as whatever every name in that function is.
A destination holding a name that is away is let through though that destination is rooted.
A root read as data rather than as a prefix writes nothing here.
The refusal names the line the write sits on.
A destination is judged only where the destination spells a name to judge.
An ignored folder is named where a whole part of the path is that folder.
An ignored ending is named where a part of the path ends there.
A name that is away is away everywhere in its file whatever that name holds there.
A `.gitignore` below the root is read by nothing here.
A write another module makes for this one is seen by nothing here.
A root a caller hands in under a name other than `root` is no checkout root.
A name a destructuring pattern binds is no rooted name and no spelled name.
A parameter's name is no rooted name and no spelled name.
A name a `for` declaration binds is no rooted name and no spelled name.
A write from a language other than TypeScript is not judged.
An un-ignoring rule drops the whole ignored name it reaches rather than only the path it names.
A descriptor is a write where its flag spells one, and a flag that is no spelled name is no write.

definition: the check refusing code outside the changes that writes into the repository
